title: Arcseconds to Ground Distance Calculator
description: Convert arcseconds to real ground distance with the Arcseconds to Ground Distance Calculator — latitude-aware, in metres and feet. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, at New York's latitude one arcsecond of latitude is 30.85 metres of ground, while one arcsecond of longitude covers only 23.46 metres — the same angle, two different distances.
quick_answer: The Arcseconds to Ground Distance Calculator converts an angle in arcseconds into the ground distance it spans, accounting for whether it runs north-south or east-west and at what latitude. Enter the arcseconds and read metres or feet — the conversion that turns chart precision into real-world size.

faq: What does this tool calculate?
The ground length of an angular span given in arcseconds, using WGS84 ellipsoid geometry at your latitude and direction.
Is the calculation done locally?
Yes — browser-side, instantly, on the values you enter.
How accurate is the result?
Ellipsoid-accurate for the stated latitude — far beyond the precision of any consumer coordinate you would apply it to.
Which datum do these coordinate tools use?
WGS84 throughout this site's coordinate family.
Do more decimal places always mean better accuracy?
No — resolution is not accuracy. One arcsecond is about 31 metres however many decimals dress it.
North-south or east-west — why the difference?
Meridians converge toward the poles, shrinking east-west spans; north-south spans ride the (nearly constant) meridian radius. Direction is an input, not a detail.
Minutes instead of seconds?
One arcminute is sixty arcseconds — about 1.85 km north-south (one nautical mile of latitude, by design).
Feet available?
Yes — imperial output alongside metric, per this site's US/Europe-first convention.
At the pole?
Longitude arcseconds collapse to zero; latitude arcseconds remain ~31 m. The calculator handles the honest extremes.
Can I invert it (metres to arcseconds)?
Divide by the per-second figure for your latitude from the table — or use the latitude/longitude degree-distance tools for the degree-scale version.
Survey-grade?
The geometry is ellipsoid-true; legal surveying adds local datums and field procedure. Use this for planning and understanding with confidence.
